title: Nine Films. Four Fridays. ₹1,400 Crore. June Is Bollywood's Bloodbath.
excerpt: Bollywood crammed an entire year's ambition into one month. From Ram Charan's record-breaking Peddi to Shahid Kapoor's Cocktail 2 and Akshay Kumar's comeback comedy, here's your complete guide to the most competitive month Indian cinema has ever seen.
body:
Bollywood has a scheduling problem. And by "problem," I mean it just detonated nine major releases into four consecutive Fridays like a fireworks factory that caught fire.

Between March and May, Hindi cinema managed exactly five significant theatrical releases in twelve weeks. *Dhurandhar: The Revenge* in March. *Bhooth Bangla* in April. *Raja Shivaji*, *Pati Patni Aur Woh Do*, and *Chand Mera Dil* across May. That's one film every two-and-a-half weeks — a gentle trickle that let each movie breathe, find its audience, and hold screens.

June said: hold my chai.

Nine films. Four weeks. Over ₹1,400 crore at stake, according to **Bollywood Hungama** estimates. Trade analysts aren't celebrating. They're bracing for impact.

> "There will be *maara-maari* for screens, as it's said in the trade." — Taran Adarsh

Here's everything you need to know about the most stacked month in Indian cinema history.

## Week 1 (June 4–5): The Opening Salvo

**Peddi** arrived like a freight train. **Ram Charan's** sports-action drama, directed by Buchi Babu Sana with an **A.R. Rahman** score, crossed ₹233 crore worldwide in just four days. It opened at ₹110 crore worldwide on Day 1 alone — the second-biggest opening of Charan's career after *RRR*. In North America, it stormed past $3 million, surpassing the lifetime totals of *Guntur Kaaram*, *SyeRaa*, and *Pushpa* in 72 hours.

The film isn't without controversy — director Buchi Babu publicly apologised for certain scenes involving **Janhvi Kapoor's** character after audience backlash — but the numbers are speaking louder than the discourse. The ₹300 crore worldwide mark looks very achievable.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZF8i7rv2Sz/

Sharing the June 5 slot: **Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai**, David Dhawan's reportedly final directorial starring **Varun Dhawan**, **Mrunal Thakur**, and **Pooja Hegde**. The old-school rom-com opened to ₹8.65 crore and is tracking toward a ₹23–25 crore opening weekend — respectable for a mid-budget comedy, but already fighting Peddi for screens. **Bobby Deol's** *Bandar* also released the same week, though it opened to a bare ₹0.5 crore.

## Week 2 (June 12): The Prestige Showdown

This is where June gets dangerous. Four films, one Friday.

**Main Vaapas Aaunga** is the headliner — Imtiaz Ali's partition-era love story starring **Diljit Dosanjh**, **Sharvari**, and **Vedang Raina**, with music by **A.R. Rahman** and lyrics by **Irshad Kamil**. The promotional campaign has been extraordinary: Rahman just performed at the Attari Border on June 7 in a first-of-its-kind tribute to BSF personnel. If Imtiaz finds the emotional frequency he hit with *Rockstar* and *Tamasha*, this could be the film of the month.

**Governor** brings **Manoj Bajpayee** into the ring — and in a year where audiences are rewarding intensity and gravitas, Bajpayee is the bankable dark horse.

**Bharat Bhagya Vidhata** is **Kangana Ranaut's** 26/11 thriller. Love her or loathe her, Kangana in a political thriller always guarantees conversation, if not always tickets.

And lurking in the corner: **Haunted 3D: Echoes of the Past**, Vikram Bhatt's horror entry starring Mahaakshay Chakraborty. It'll fight for whatever screens the other three leave behind.

## Week 3 (June 19): The Big Bet

**Cocktail 2** has the week to itself — and it needs every screen it can get. **Shahid Kapoor**, **Kriti Sanon**, and **Rashmika Mandanna** headline this sequel to the 2012 hit that turned Deepika Padukone into a superstar. It's already the most anticipated Indian film on IMDb and has reportedly recovered half its ₹150 crore budget from pre-release business alone.

The original *Cocktail* was a sleeper hit that spoke to urban India — the kind of film diaspora audiences adopted as their own. If the sequel captures even half that lightning, it could be June's biggest winner.

But it won't have the theatres to itself for long. This is also the week **Toy Story 5** goes wide internationally, and Steven Spielberg's **Disclosure Day** is lurking.

## Week 4 (June 26): The Nostalgia Play

**Welcome to the Jungle** closes June with maximum star wattage: **Akshay Kumar**, **Suniel Shetty**, **Raveena Tandon**, and **Arshad Warsi**. It's a sequel to the 2007 *Welcome* and its 2014 follow-up *Welcome Back* — franchise comedy that prints money on name recognition alone.

For Akshay Kumar, it's a critical release. After *Bhooth Bangla* earned a decent ₹291 crore worldwide, a strong follow-up would confirm his commercial resurgence. For Shetty and Tandon, both deep in comeback arcs, it's a chance to remind audiences why they were stars in the first place.

Also arriving June 26: the DCU's **Supergirl** and the **Masters of the Universe** reboot. Hollywood isn't ceding June to Bollywood without a fight.

## For the Diaspora: Your Survival Guide

If you're outside India, here's what matters:

- **Peddi** is already playing in US, UK, Canada, and Australia. Telugu version is dominant; Hindi dub is in select screens.
- **Main Vaapas Aaunga** (June 12) will have wide international release — Diljit's star power guarantees North American screens.
- **Cocktail 2** (June 19) will play wide internationally. Hindi only.
- **Welcome to the Jungle** (June 26) — expect strong diaspora play; the franchise has built-in NRI nostalgia.
- Most films will hit OTT 6–8 weeks after theatrical release. JioHotstar, Netflix, and Amazon Prime are the likely landing spots.

## The Real Story

The stampede isn't random. Bollywood's theatrical model is under siege. The 8-week OTT window has trained audiences to wait rather than watch. Producers are racing to release before the monsoon kills footfall and before streaming makes the trip to the theatre feel optional.

> "Every producer is of the opinion that 'Main kyun aage jaau?'" — Taran Adarsh

Nobody wants to blink first. So nobody blinks at all. And June becomes a war zone where ₹1,400 crore is on the table and every film is fighting for the same 4,000-odd screens.

Some will win. Some will be forgotten by July. But for four Fridays, Bollywood is going to feel like it used to — loud, crowded, and completely alive.

*All box office figures are estimates based on trade reports as of June 8, 2026.*
